record.title: Turn-level action selection improves reported agent success with substantial token overhead
record.summary: A 4 November arXiv preprint evaluates turn-level best-of-N (Turn-BoN): at each step, a generator proposes 4 or 8 candidate tool actions and a separate language-model selector chooses one before it is executed. On 89 Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks across four trials, the authors report higher pass rates for Qwen3.6-35B and K2-Horizon-375B generators when paired with Kimi-K3 or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash selectors. Reported gains include K2-Horizon 73.3% to 77.9% at N=4 and Qwen3.6 47.5% to 52.8% at N=4 or 55.2% at N=8. The authors also report 40–50% fewer turns and reduced looping, while output tokens rise to about 3.6–8.2 times baseline. These preliminary paper-reported results use two generator models and stronger selectors; they were not independently reproduced.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors submitted arXiv:2611.06868v1 on 4 November 2026, describing turn-level best-of-N action selection for language-model agents.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On 89 Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks over four trials, the authors report K2-Horizon-375B pass@1 rising from 73.3% to 77.9% with N=4, and Qwen3.6-35B rising from 47.5% to 52.8% with N=4 or 55.2% with N=8 when paired with Kimi-K3 or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash selectors.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that the tested Turn-BoN configurations used approximately 3.6–8.2 times the baseline output tokens per attempt; they also report about 40–50% fewer turns on average.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish independent reproduction, generalization beyond the tested Terminal-Bench setup, benefits with equal or weaker selectors, or a net cost/performance advantage across real deployments.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the pass-rate, consistency, behavior or compute findings was reviewed.
The reviewed arXiv page did not identify an inspected code or task-trace release.
The reported selector models are more capable than the generators in the chosen setup; equal or weaker selectors were not tested.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated across tasks and model pairings, per-turn action selection could be a useful inference-time scaling method for interactive agents, but the reported gains require about 3.6–8.2 times baseline output tokens and are limited to two generator model families and one benchmark. This score reflects potential utility, not confidence.
limitations: All reported task and compute results are author claims from a preprint; no independent reproduction was performed.

The study tests two generator model families on 89 Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks with four trials and stronger selector models; it does not establish how gains behave with weaker or equal-capability selectors.
The reported 3.6–8.2x total output-token overhead is not a billed-cost or latency comparison across deployed systems.
brief.summary: A 4 November arXiv preprint evaluates turn-level best-of-N (Turn-BoN): at each step, a generator proposes 4 or 8 candidate tool actions and a separate language-model selector chooses one before it is executed. On 89 Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks across four trials, the authors report higher pass rates for Qwen3.6-35B and K2-Horizon-375B generators when paired with Kimi-K3 or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash selectors. Reported gains include K2-Horizon 73.3% to 77.9% at N=4 and Qwen3.6 47.5% to 52.8% at N=4 or 55.2% at N=8. The authors also report 40–50% fewer turns and reduced looping, while output tokens rise to about 3.6–8.2 times baseline. technical.claimed_result: The authors report higher pass rates, fewer turns/loops and output-token use about 3.6–8.2 times baseline on the stated setup.
technical.compute_or_cost: Authors report total output tokens at about 3.6x–8.2x baseline per attempt. The paper does not establish real-world billed cost or latency advantage.
technical.demonstrated_result: The authors published a versioned preprint, its method, tables and claims; no task outcome was independently established in this activation.
technical.mechanism: At each interaction state, sample N next tool actions from a generator model; a separate LLM selector receives the task and history plus the candidate actions, selects one, and only that action is executed.
technical.regime: Two generator models, stronger selector models, 89 Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks, four trials, and N=4 or 8.
technical.reproducibility: No independent rerun or public artifact audit performed; paper is preliminary.
technical.strongest_baseline: The same generator model in the mini-SWE-agent/Terminal-Bench setup without a selector; authors report four trials and 89 tasks.

brief.title: Turn-level action selection improves reported agent success with substantial token overhead
brief.why_it_matters: Turn-BoN offers a simple way to steer interactive agents by selecting among candidate actions at every step, and the paper reports gains in task success and fewer looping behaviors. Its measured token overhead is substantial, and the small setup with stronger selector models does not establish a general capability or cost-effective deployment advantage.
